success: The retention/anonymisation path is added ADDITIVELY: a later migration widens audit_events_append_only() with CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, which migrate-lint's destructive pattern does not match, so the migration needs no -- allow-destructive: annotation provided it never contains the bare word TRUNCATE (migrate-lint matches every line except a whole-line `--` comment, which it skips: a trailing `-- …` comment and every function-body line ARE matched, so a widened body that names TG_OP = 'TRUNCATE' must instead refuse by default, or carry the annotation; vizra-core scripts/migrate-lint.sh at main 36a72df, the `--*) continue` comment skip); the row trigger and statement-level TRUNCATE trigger stay in place
A retention sweep removes or anonymises rows older than the retention window only through that path, in batches, and writes one audit row per run naming the window and the count, never row contents

Account erasure (VZ-ACCOUNT-002) scrubs and tombstones the users row — email NULLed (users.email is NOT NULL in vizra-core migration 0005, so this first needs an additive ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email DROP NOT NULL, which migrate-lint does not flag and 0005 anticipates), username replaced with a unique, non-identifying handle of 3–30 ASCII characters that satisfies users_username_shape (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,29}$) and the case-folded unique index users_username_fold_key (vizra-core migration 0005) — so neither a constant placeholder (it collides on the second erasure) nor `erased-` + a full 32-hex UUID (39 characters, over the shape) will do, and an erasure test erases two users in sequence, credentials removed, tombstoned_at set — and anonymises that user's username in the audit rows that name them; actor_user_id still references the tombstoned row, so the audit chain stays intact
negative: Every UPDATE or DELETE on audit_events other than the retention/anonymisation shape is still refused by the trigger, and TRUNCATE is still refused; a controlled mutation that widens the function to accept any UPDATE turns a named test red
DELETE FROM users for a user named by an audit row fails (audit_events_actor_user_fk is ON DELETE RESTRICT, 23503); the erasure path never issues DELETE on users, and a test asserts it
No API route exposes arbitrary audit mutation; the retention and erasure jobs are the only callers of the anonymisation path
privacy: audit before, after and actor_label never carry an email address or any PII beyond the username; a test scans every audit kind the suite writes for email-shaped values and fails on any

Because actor_user_id still joins audit rows to users, erasure scrubs or replaces users.username itself, not only the username copied into audit rows; anonymisation also clears ip_prefix; after erasure the user's original username, email and credentials are not reachable from the audit read surface (directly or through the actor_user_id join), exports or logs; an erasure test asserts users.email, users.username and credentials hold no original value
recovery: The erasure job is resumable and idempotent: a crash between scrub and tombstone re-runs to the same end state, and re-running on a tombstoned user is a no-op
An interrupted retention sweep resumes without skipping or double-counting; each batch and its audit row commit in one transaction
Tombstoning the owner leaves the instance recoverable (users_one_owner counts only live owners; recovery path under VZ-ADMIN-USERS-001)
